## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}

- Mobile responsive; touch controls for orbit; safe areas.

Network works. We'll build a Vite app (projectType supports vite). Install three and @mediapipe/tasks-vision. Vendor wasm + models into public/.

Design details.

Architecture:
- index.html: shell with UI.
- src/main.js: bootstraps app, renderer, camera, scene, loop.
- src/tracking.js: MediaPipe landmarkers wrapper, camera, inference.
- src/avatar.js: 3D skeleton/avatar rig built from primitives.
- src/face.js: face mesh points, eyes/mouth.
- src/hands.js: hands.
- src/demo.js: synthetic pose generator.
- src/ui.js maybe.
- src/style.css.

Maybe simpler to keep manageable but high-quality. Let's think about correctness of MediaPipe usage.

```js
import { FilesetResolver, PoseLandmarker, FaceLandmarker, HandLandmarker } from '@mediapipe/tasks-vision';

const vision = await FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks('/wasm');
pose = await PoseLandmarker.createFromOptions(vision, {
  baseOptions: { modelAssetPath: '/models/pose_landmarker_lite.task', delegate: 'GPU' },
  runningMode: 'VIDEO',
  numPoses: 1,
  minPoseDetectionConfidence: 0.5,
  minPosePresenceConfidence: 0.5,
  minTrackingConfidence: 0.5,
  outputSegmentationMasks: false,
});
```
Face: outputFaceBlendshapes: true, outputFacialTransformationMatrixes: true.
Hand: numHands: 2, minHandDetectionConfidence, minHandPresenceConfidence, minTrackingConfidence.

Detection loop: requestAnimationFrame or setInterval ~30fps. `detectForVideo(video, performance.now())` only when video.currentTime changed. Run all three per frame, maybe stagger face every frame; performance should be fine (GPU).

Coordinates:
- Pose worldLandmarks: meters, hip-centered, y-up? MediaPipe world landmarks: x right, y down? In world coordinates, y is down (I think origin at hips, y down). Actually MediaPipe pose world landmarks are in meters with origin at the center of hips, and y-axis points down? Documentation: "real-world 3D coordinates in meters with the origin at the center between hips." Axes probably same orientation as image: x right, y down, z toward camera negative? Common usage in Three.js requires negating y and z. Many examples: `position.set(-lm.x, -lm.y, -lm.z)` for normalized. For world landmarks, use x, -y, -z. We'll calibrate visually via screenshot? Hard without actual human in webcam in headless. Demo mode will use synthetic landmarks in our own coordinate system, so we need consistency.

Better approach: Use pose worldLandmarks for 3D body; map (x, y, z) -> Three.js (x, -y, -z) so y up and z toward viewer positive. Then center torso. Scale maybe 1 unit per meter, camera at z=3.

For demo mode, generate world landmarks in meters using a rig definition (same landmark indices). We can generate synthetic humanoid motion: jumping jacks/wave/dance. That also proves app functions without camera.

Avatar design: Rather than a humanoid mesh with skinning, a stylized "holographic mannequin": glowing capsule limbs between joints, sphere joints, torso shape, head with face mesh. This reads well as 3D body tracking. Could also add an abstract particle avatar. Use `MeshStandardMaterial` with emissive + bloom (UnrealBloomPass via EffectComposer) for a premium look. But postprocessing bloom on SwiftShader may be slow. Could use additive wireframe without postprocessing. But we can use a subtle bloom via composer maybe. Better performance: no postprocessing, use emissive materials, fog, and additive line glows. We can still achieve a nice look with gradient background, grid, reflections.

Visual concept: "KINETIC — Real-time motion capture" dark studio with cyan/violet neon skeleton. Camera feed in a rounded PIP bottom-right (or left). 3D viewport full screen. Left top brand. Top center tracking chips. Right side layer toggles. Bottom left metrics (FPS, latency, joint count). Bottom center start camera button / status.

Actually for a TikTok-like app, the visual might be a person with 3D effects. Let's make it striking.

Avatar:
- Pelvis/hip center.
- Torso: use a stretched capsule or custom lathe? We can create a "torso" mesh that connects shoulders and hips: a rounded box scaled and oriented based on shoulder/hip vectors. Simplest: a set of "bone" capsules:
  - spine: pelvis→neck
  - shoulders: neck→left/right shoulder
  - upper arms, forearms, hands (hands as hand skeleton).
  - hips: pelvis→left/right hip
  - thighs, shins, feet.
- Joint spheres at key landmarks (shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles).
- Head: sphere or rounded head with face points overlaid.
- Feet: glowing boxes oriented along foot direction using heel/toe landmarks.

Use worldLandmarks indices:
0 nose, 11 L shoulder, 12 R shoulder, 13 L elbow, 14 R elbow, 15 L wrist, 16 R wrist, 17-22 hands, 23 L hip, 24 R hip, 25 L knee, 26 R knee, 27 L ankle, 28 R ankle, 29 L heel, 30 R heel, 31 L foot index, 32 R foot index. Note MediaPipe's left/right are person's left/right, mirrored on screen. Fine.

Bone radii tapered: create cylinder/capsule geometry per bone with dynamic scale/position/quaternion. Use one CapsuleGeometry(1,1,4,8) base and scale (r, len/2?, r). CapsuleGeometry(radius, length) with length as cylinder part. Simpler use CylinderGeometry(1,1,1,8) oriented Y and scale x,z by radius, y by length. Add sphere at joints. Glow shell? Use `MeshBasicMaterial` transparent additive for glow plus solid standard material.

To avoid too many materials, share materials.

Body avatar should smoothly follow. Use exponential smoothing on landmark positions per index, with adaptive alpha. For tracking jitter, a simple One Euro filter would be great. Implement a small OneEuroFilter for 3D vectors. On new landmark: filter each axis. Face has 478 points; filtering all is heavy but okay; maybe render face mesh only relative to head and smooth head transform only, while face points follow with lighter smoothing. We can render face mesh in head local coordinates from face landmarks, but MediaPipe face landmarks are in normalized image coords, not head-relative. We can convert face landmarks to head-local by subtracting nose/forehead center and scaling. That would look like a face mask attached to the 3D head, but won't reflect actual head rotation in 3D (no depth). FaceLandmarker gives facial transformation matrix, which can provide head pose. We can use that to orient the head and render face mesh in local coordinates. That's a nice touch.

Alternatively, render face mesh as 3D points computed from face landmarks normalized coords mapped to a plane, but with z from landmarks (relative). Use orthographic projection? Face landmarks z is relative depth. We can build face point cloud in head-local coords: x = (lm.x - cx)*scale, y = -(lm.y - cy)*scale, z = -lm.z*scale. Then rotate by head matrix from faceLandmarker. Hmm matrix transforms canonical face to camera. We can extract rotation and apply. But it's extra complexity. Simpler and robust: build face mesh relative to head anchor from pose (nose/ears), with landmarks normalized to face bounding box, apply as a decal on head sphere. Eye and mouth contours glow based on blendshapes. Head orientation derived from pose ears/shoulders, which gives decent 3D.

But "face movement" should visibly track mouth/eyes. We'll render:
- Face point cloud (468 points) as small cyan points, with eye contours highlighted in white/cyan, lips highlighted in pink.
- Eye blink: scale eye highlights based on eyeBlinkLeft/Right blendshapes; mouth open: scale mouth ring based on jawOpen; smile: curvature from mouthSmileLeft/Right.
- Iris points (468-477) as bright dots that move — track gaze! Use iris landmarks from face mesh and map to head-local positions. Great for "eyes movement".
- Mouth interior? Highlight lips with color intensity based on jawOpen and mouth smile.

Use FaceLandmarker 478 landmarks. Build face geometry once: point cloud with positions from canonical face layout? We need a stable mapping from normalized face landmarks to 3D local positions. Since face landmarks in image space change with head rotation, but if we center and normalize by inter-ocular distance, it looks okay. The face point cloud will track expression and gaze in 3D-ish. Attach to head anchor in avatar. It may jitter but smooth.

Maybe better to render face overlay in a separate "face inset" panel? No, keep in 3D.

Hands:
- 21 landmarks each with 3D worldLandmarks. Render bones as cylinders + joint spheres. Attach at wrist? MediaPipe hand worldLandmarks are in meters centered at hand geometric center, not connected to pose. To place hands on avatar, we can translate the hand landmarks so that hand landmark 0 (wrist) aligns with pose wrist position (if pose wrist visible), and orient using the vector from hand wrist to middle MCP relative to pose forearm. Since both are in similar world scale, simplest: offset = poseWrist - handWrist, then apply each hand point + offset. Orientation may not match arm but position will. Alternatively use hand landmarks normalized relative to pose wrist, preserving hand orientation from camera. The hand worldLandmarks axes align with camera; pose world axes also camera-aligned, so offset only is fine. Good.

If pose wrist not visible but hand is, position hand relative to face/torso using normalized coords mapped into view? For simplicity, if pose unavailable, place hands at fixed sides. Demo mode handles synthetic.

Feet:
- Use pose ankles/heels/toe indices, render foot bones and glowing foot pads. Also foot "confidence" chip based on visibility.

Face positioning:
- Use pose landmarks 0 (nose), 7/8 (ears). Head center = midpoint of ears or nose + offset. We can build a head group at midpoint between ears, oriented from ear axis. Scale head size = distance between ears. Render head as a sphere with radius ~ ear distance * 0.55. Face point cloud placed in front of head center. Head group rotation: build basis with x axis = left ear→right ear, y up = from nose to top? We can approximate using shoulders. Simpler: head group at nose with orientation identity and face points built in head-local coords. Since pose is in 3D, the head moves and rotates via ear axis; construct quaternion aligning local x to ear axis and local y to "up" computed from ear midpoint to nose? Let's do:
  - earMid = (earL+earR)/2.
  - xAxis = normalize(earR - earL) (person's right).
  - upHint = normalize(earMid - (shoulderMid)) (up).
  - zAxis = normalize(cross(xAxis, upHint)) maybe toward camera.
  - yAxis = cross(zAxis, xAxis).
  - quaternion from basis.
  - Head center = earMid + upHint * headRadius*0.5? Actually earMid is at ear level, center of head slightly above? Nose is lower. Put head center at earMid.
  - Face points in local coords: from face landmarks normalized relative to face center. Face landmarks x right, y down, z toward camera? Use x=(lm.x-cx)*faceWidth, y=-(lm.y-cy)*faceWidth, z=-lm.z*faceWidth. This plane faces +z in local head space. If head basis z axis points toward camera, good.

But face landmark bounding box in image includes head rotation, so it will distort, but acceptable stylized.

Alternative use facial transformation matrix to get true 3D face mesh in camera space and transform into world? Too complex to map into avatar, but we could render the face mesh independently in 3D at head location using matrix rotation. Not needed.

Demo mode: Since headless verification won't have a person, generate synthetic pose landmarks. Need to render a convincing humanoid. Define landmark positions for a standing human in meters, then animate:
- A dance loop with arms waving, knees bending, head turning, hands and feet.
- Face: generate face landmark positions from a canonical template? We can synthesize a simplified face point cloud: use actual canonical face landmark positions? We could download the face landmarker model but not canonical mesh. We can create a procedural face: ring contours for eyes, eyebrows, lips, plus face oval points and iris. For demo mode, generate 478 points procedurally in head-local coords. But real tracking uses actual 478 points. Could generate a face template procedurally for demo: grid of points on an ellipsoid face, plus eye rings, lips, etc. Then animate eyes (iris position), mouth open (lip separation), blink (eyelid). This also gives a good face visualization when no camera. We can build a template once with 478 points? We don't need exactly 478; face renderer can accept a point list plus semantic indices (for contours) if real data; for demo use a separate generated mesh. Simpler: build the face visualization from semantic groups (face oval, left/right eye, iris, lips, brows, nose) using landmark indices for real mode; for demo, build same groups from synthetic positions. Hmm.

Maybe better: for both modes, render face as a "mesh" using triangle indices from MediaPipe FACE_LANDMARKS_TESSELATION? tasks-vision exports FaceLandmarker.FACE_LANDMARKS_TESSELATION? I recall `FaceLandmarker.FACE_LANDMARKS_TESSELATION` is available in @mediapipe/tasks-vision (connections). Yes, tasks-vision exposes `FaceLandmarker.FACE_LANDMARKS_TESSELATION`, `FACE_LANDMARKS_LIPS`, etc. We can use line segments for contours, and points for tesselation. For demo, we could use actual face geometry from a generated canonical face. But we can also just use a generic face mask (wireframe) with synthetic animation.

For the screenshot, demo mode is what will show. Need it to look excellent.

Maybe use a downloaded 3D head model (GLB) from Sketchfab? There's a skill for that, but complexity and licensing. Procedural stylized mannequin is safer. A holographic mannequin with no face texture but glowing facial features can look very cool.

Let's design the avatar as a stylized "wireframe mannequin":
- Body bones as glowing capsules with dark glass inner material.
- Head as a faceted icosahedron wireframe with a glowing face point cloud.
- Hands as detailed skeletons.
- Feet as glowing wedges.
- A circular platform under the feet with pulsing rings.
- Particle field around body responding to movement.
- Motion trails: afterimage ghosts? Could add subtle trailing rings when limbs move fast. Maybe not necessary.

UI:
- Font: use Google Fonts? Offline maybe. Use system fonts with `font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ...`; can download font files or use CDN. Better self-host? Google Fonts fetch at runtime works but may not in preview. Use CSS import? We'll include a font via npm? Simpler use system `ui-sans-serif` but with letterspacing; looks fine. Could download Space Grotesk woff2 from Google and vendor. Let's do that for polish (two weights). Use fonts from fonts.gstatic.com.

- Colors: near-black #05070c, cyan #5ff5ff, violet #a78bfa, magenta #ff4ecd, lime for status.

Layout:
- Full-bleed 3D canvas.
- Header: logo mark (animated rings) + "KINETIC" + "MOTION LAB"; right: status pill "LIVE" / "DEMO", settings icons.
- Left panel: "TRACKING MATRIX" with rows BODY/FACE/HANDS/FEET/EYES/MOUTH and bars/values. This satisfies explicit tracking of all parts.
- Right panel: layer toggles (Avatar, Body, Face, Hands, Feet, Trails), and camera controls (Start camera, demo).
- Bottom left: metrics FPS, latency, joints.
- Bottom right: camera PIP with overlay and "CAMERA OFF / DEMO FEED" label.
- Center bottom: hint "Drag to orbit · Scroll to zoom" and button "Enable camera".

For mobile: stack panels, hide right panel behind a gear? Ensure not cluttered. Media queries.

Interaction:
- OrbitControls with damping, auto-rotate when idle.
- Start camera button requests getUserMedia; on success, hide demo and begin inference. On failure, show toast and stay in demo.
- Toggles for layers.
- Keyboard shortcuts: C camera, D demo, 1-5 layers, R reset view.
- Fullscreen button.
- "Record" maybe not needed. TikTok-like app could have "Record 3D" but we can't easily. Skip.

Add a cinematic intro overlay? A brief loading screen with logo while models load. Then fade. For screenshot, ensure it's gone. In demo mode, models load in background but the demo starts immediately. Good.

Performance: Three.js + MediaPipe. We can lazy-load MediaPipe only when camera enabled. But tracking status should show demo values. Demo starts immediately, models load in background only if camera requested. Actually if camera not started, don't load models at all. That makes initial load fast. Camera button triggers model loading with progress UI.

Need to vendor assets:
- Copy wasm folder from node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/wasm to public/wasm.
- Download models to public/models.

Vite copies public to dist. Model sizes ~17MB; build okay. The server serves wasm MIME.

Important: For `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks('/wasm')` with Vite base './', absolute path '/wasm' works at root but if deployed under a subpath, base './' matters. Use `import.meta.env.BASE_URL + 'wasm'`. Vite BASE_URL is './' when built with --base ./. FilesetResolver will fetch './wasm/vision_wasm_internal.js' relative to page. Should be okay. Model path also `new URL('models/...', import.meta.url)`? public assets referenced with BASE_URL. Use `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}models/pose_landmarker_lite.task`.

Potential issue: tasks-vision wasm loader may use `importScripts` / dynamic import; with base './' and relative paths, should work. Test in browser.

Now let's implement. First scaffold package.json, install deps, copy assets.

Let's think through the 3D math and avatar code carefully.

Coordinate mapping:
- World landmarks (pose): origin hips, y down. Map to Three: X = lm.x, Y = -lm.y, Z = -lm.z. Then hips at ~0. Camera at (0, 0.4, 3.4) looking at (0, 0, 0)? The body's hips at 0, head at ~0.6, feet at ~-0.9. So center target ~0.
- Actually scale: worldLandmarks meters. Body height ~1.7m. Camera at (0, 0.1, 3.2) FOV 40. Good. Add platform at y=-0.95.
- For normalized landmarks fallback, map x and y into view; but use world only. If worldLandmarks missing, skip body.

Smoothing:
- OneEuroFilter per landmark axis. 33*3 = 99 filters. Fine. Face 478*3 = 1434 filters, fine but heavier; we can smooth face group positions with simple lerp because face landmarks relative. Hands 42*3. Fine.
- Implement filter with minCutoff 1.2, beta 0.02? For motion capture, OneEuro standard: freq=30, minCutoff=1.0, beta=0.007, dCutoff=1.0. For 3D positions in meters, beta maybe 0.5? OneEuro beta depends on units. Values ~0.1-1.0. Use minCutoff=1.5, beta=0.3. Jitter at rest smoothed; fast motion responsive.

But demo mode doesn't need filter.

Body rig:
- Define bones with landmark pairs and radii:
  - spine: 23/24 midpoint → 11/12 midpoint (torso), radius 0.13
  - chest: shoulder midpoint → neck (nose? use midpoint of ears? neck index 11/12 midpoint + up). We can add a neck bone from shoulderMid to head center.
  - shoulderL: shoulderMid? Actually bones from 11 to 12 across shoulders.
  - upperArmL 11→13 r .055; forearm 13→15 r .045; hand handled separately.
  - hips: 23→24 r .10; thigh 23→25 r .075; shin 25→27 r .06; foot 27→31 r .05 (or ankle→toe).
  - head: sphere at headCenter radius.
- Torso mesh: custom capsule between hipMid and shoulderMid with radius ~0.16; plus chest ellipsoid. Maybe a tapered "torso" built from LatheGeometry or CapsuleGeometry scaled x=1.4,z=0.8. Use a capsule oriented along spine, scale x 1.5, z 0.9. Looks like a torso. Add chest plate: rounded box? Use CapsuleGeometry with radius 0.16, length 0.35. We'll create a Group at midpoint, orient along spine, scale x 1.5, z 0.75. Good.
- Pelvis: sphere scaled (0.18, 0.12, 0.12).
- Head: `IcosahedronGeometry(1, 2)` with wireframe overlay and a translucent inner. Scale by headRadius (~0.115). Maybe stylized faceted.
- Joint spheres at 11,12,13,14,15,16,23,24,25,26,27,28 plus maybe 0? Use radius 0.03.
- Feet: create a wedge mesh (BoxGeometry) oriented from ankle to toe, scale length. Or use a custom foot shape: rounded box 0.09 x 0.05 x 0.22. Place at midpoint of ankle and toe, orient with quaternion from direction. Add glowing toe line. Use same approach as bones but a box. Feet have their own group for toggling.
- Hands: separate class.

Body materials:
- `boneMat`: MeshStandardMaterial color #0b1a22, emissive #18e6ff, emissiveIntensity 0.55, metalness .4, roughness .25. With additive glow shell? Add duplicate cylinder with MeshBasicMaterial color cyan, transparent, opacity .12, blending Additive, scale 1.8. That creates a halo. This doubles draw calls but fine (~20 bones).
- Joints: MeshBasicMaterial cyan/white.
- Torso: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission? expensive. Use standard with transparent opacity 0.65 and emissive. Add wireframe overlay.
- Color palette: cyan for body, violet for face, magenta for hands, lime for feet? The TikTok style maybe neon. Keep coherent: body cyan, face violet, hands magenta, feet lime/amber. Tracking chips matching colors. Eyes bright white, mouth pink.

Particles:
- 600 points in a cylinder around the body, slowly drifting, color cyan/violet, size .01. Use PointsMaterial with additive blending, transparent, opacity .6. Animate rotation and react to motion energy.
- Platform: ring geometries (RingGeometry) at y=-0.98, rotated -PI/2, with additive materials, pulsing scale/opacity. Also a grid helper (fog fade) maybe `GridHelper` with dark cyan lines. Grid 20x20 at y=-0.98.
- Backdrop: large sphere with shader gradient? Simpler scene.background = color and fog. Add radial gradient CSS behind canvas; renderer alpha true so CSS gradient shows. But fog needs background color. We can set renderer alpha and use scene.fog with color matching. Maybe use a giant plane with shader gradient? Or `scene.background = new THREE.Color('#04060a')`, plus a big backdrop sphere with ShaderMaterial gradient (top #0a1220, bottom #020306). Use `BackSide` sphere. Good.

Bloom: Could add UnrealBloomPass for neon glow. With 3D scene and SwiftShader, might be slow. Use selective bloom? Too complex. Emissive + additive glow shells should be enough. Maybe use a cheap custom bloom via `EffectComposer` with RenderPass + UnrealBloomPass at half res. Let's test performance in headless screenshot only (not real-time), but mobile performance matters. We can add bloom toggle off on low-end. Hmm, use no composer; rely on CSS `filter`? No.

Let's use UnrealBloomPass with strength 0.6, radius 0.4, threshold 0.6, resolution scaled. It gives a premium look. On integrated GPUs, 1080p bloom is okay-ish. On mobile maybe heavy. We can detect and disable on mobile (window.innerWidth < 720) and allow toggle. Since screenshot is desktop, bloom on. Add renderer pixelRatio min(devicePixelRatio, 2).

Face rendering:
- Real mode:
  - face landmarks are normalized image coords. Compute face center from landmark 1 (nose tip? index 1 is nose tip; 4 is nose tip actually? MediaPipe face mesh: 1 nose tip, 4 nose tip? Let's recall: 1 = nose tip? Canonical face mesh: 1 is nose tip, 4 is nose tip bottom? Common: 1 nose tip, 4 nose tip, 6 between eyes, 10 forehead, 152 chin, 234 left cheek, 454 right cheek. Use bounding box of all points to get center and size. Build local coords:
    cx = (minX+maxX)/2, cy=(minY+maxY)/2, s = max(width, height) in normalized coords. For a head of radius R (~0.12m), face width ~ 0.11m. local x = (lm.x - cx)/s * R*2.2; local y = -(lm.y - cy)/s * R*2.2; local z = -lm.z/s * R*2.2 (MediaPipe z relative to x scale; negative z toward camera? In face landmarks, z represents depth with smaller values closer to camera; typical visualization uses z * -1. We'll use -z and place points at head center + forward * R*0.7). Actually we want the face on the front of the head: head local +Z is forward (toward camera). Map face x to local x, image y down → local y up negative, and face z toward camera → local z maybe small positive. Set base z = R*0.9. Add `-lm.z * scale` maybe. If z is negative for closer points, -z gives positive. Good.
  - The face group is placed at head center with head quaternion. So local +Z is forward.
  - Draw tesselation lines with low opacity violet; draw points as Points with size 0.003, color #b79bff. Draw eye contours and lips brighter. Iris points (468-472 left iris, 473-477 right iris) as bright cyan/white points; the iris moves with gaze.
  - Need line geometry for tesselation. `FaceLandmarker.FACE_LANDMARKS_TESSELATION` is an array of {start,end} connections. Build BufferGeometry position array each frame from pairs. That's ~2556 connections, updating 15336 floats per frame; fine. Use LineSegments with additive material. Or use a static index geometry and update positions. Build once with indices.
  - Face points: BufferGeometry with 478 positions updated per frame.
  - Eye/lip lines similarly use connection arrays. Build separate line segments.

## Objective
- Build a browser app that tracks full body, face, hands, feet, eyes, and mouth movement in real time in 3D, inspired by a TikTok motion-capture video link the user supplied.

## Requirements
- Real-time 3D tracking of body, face, hands, feet, eyes, and mouth.
- TikTok link (`https://vt.tiktok.com/ZSgTJ8uek/`) could not be viewed; content unavailable.
- App should work in browser preview, be visually polished, and support mobile touch layouts.
- Keep tracking local; video should not be uploaded.

## Decisions
- Use MediaPipe Tasks Vision (`PoseLandmarker`, `FaceLandmarker`, `HandLandmarker`) for tracking.
- Use Three.js to render a stylized neon 3D skeleton/avatar, face mesh, hand skeletons, and foot rigs.
- Feet come from pose landmarks 27–32; eyes/mouth from face landmarks + 52 blendshapes.
- Add a synthetic demo mode so the app works without a camera and for headless screenshot verification.
- Vendor MediaPipe WASM and `.task` models locally under `public/`; use Vite with `--base ./`.
- Dynamically import `src/tracking.js` on camera start to keep initial bundle light.
- Use procedural demo face, hand, and body animation; no external GLB assets.
- Switched renderer to `antialias: false`, `alpha: false`, solid `#04070c` background to test performance; current visual may need reverting/refining.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded Vite app with `three@0.187.0`, `@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.2.0`, `vite@8.3.5`.
- Downloaded local assets: `public/wasm/*`, `public/models/{pose_landmarker_lite,face_landmarker,hand_landmarker}.task`, local fonts in `public/fonts/`.
- Built full UI shell in `index.html` and `src/style.css`: top bar, tracking matrix, face signals, energy graph, layers, input controls, PIP, mobile matrix/dock, loader, toast.
- Implemented `src/filters.js` (OneEuro/Vec3/Landmark filters), `src/demo.js` (synthetic dancer with body/hands/feet/face expressions), `src/tracking.js` (camera + MediaPipe inference + metrics), `src/face-rig.js`, `src/hand-rig.js`, `src/foot-rig.js`, `src/avatar.js`, `src/pip.js`, `src/ui.js`, `src/main.js`, `src/glow.js`.
- `npm run build` succeeds; output chunks: `index-*.js` ~623 kB, `tracking-*.js` ~160 kB.
- Dev server running in tmux session `kinetic` on `http://localhost:3000`.
- Playwright browser installed; page loads with no console errors; demo mode active; 553 tracked points shown; loader hides.
- Diagnosed severe performance issue: page renders ~1–3 FPS under SwiftShader/Xvfb. A minimal WebGL clear canvas gets ~40 FPS; blank page ~61 FPS. With all loop work monkey-patched and all HUD/FX removed, FPS reached ~60. Removing CSS animations/fx/HUD was the key fix; `.ambient`, `.grain`, `.scanlines`, `.vignette`, and HUD layers appear to be the performance bottleneck under software rendering.
- Reduced/removed `backdrop-filter`, `mix-blend-mode`, ambient blur, and added UI update caching/throttling; scene-only parts were not the bottleneck.

### Active
- Performance optimization and visual verification via Playwright screenshot. Screenshot still times out at 5s at current low FPS.
- Need to finish CSS performance cleanup (remove/replace expensive ambient/grain/scanlines/vignette layers and continuous CSS animations) while preserving the intended visual style.
- Need to visually inspect the 3D avatar, face, hands, feet, and HUD in a screenshot and iterate on aesthetics/geometry.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli screenshot` times out (`TimeoutError: page.screenshot: Timeout 5000ms exceeded`) because page FPS is ~1–3 under SwiftShader.
- TikTok reference video content is unavailable; design is an original interpretation.

## Next Move
1. Optimize `src/style.css`: remove `.grain`, simplify/remove `.ambient`, `.scanlines`, `.vignette`, large box-shadows, and continuous CSS animations; keep a single static background gradient. Re-test FPS.
2. Consider setting `renderer alpha: false` with a Three.js background gradient or restoring `alpha: true` with a lightweight CSS background after performance stabilizes.
3. Reload page, measure FPS with `playwright-cli --raw eval`, then retry `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/desktop-01.png`.
4. Inspect screenshot for avatar proportions, face mesh placement (face may be inside head sphere; `FaceRig.group.position.z = headRadius * 0.1` was added), hand/feet visibility, HUD layout, and mobile responsive layout.
5. Fix any visual defects, then test camera path (model loading, `FilesetResolver` paths, MediaPipe inference) and mobile viewport.
6. Verify production build (`npm run build`) and final screenshot; ensure loader/UI works in deployed static output.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: app loop, camera start/demo switch, model loading, debug surface `window.__kinetic`.
- `src/avatar.js`: Three.js scene, body rig, head/face attachment, hands/feet, layers, snapshot.
- `src/face-rig.js`: real MediaPipe face mesh + procedural demo face.
- `src/tracking.js`: MediaPipe initialization, camera, inference, blendshape/gaze metrics; exports `FACE_CONNECTIONS`.
- `src/demo.js`: synthetic full-body/face/hand motion generator.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD updates, cached DOM writes, energy canvas.
- `src/pip.js`: camera/demo preview overlay drawing.
- `src/style.css`: main visual/UI styling; performance hotspot.
- `index.html`: app shell and DOM structure.
- `src/hand-rig.js`: hand skeleton rendering.
- `src/foot-rig.js`: foot capsule rendering.
- `src/glow.js`: shared glow textures/materials.
- `src/filters.js`: One Euro smoothing.
- `public/models/`, `public/wasm/`: local MediaPipe assets.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a browser app that tracks full body, face, hands, feet, eyes, and mouth movement in real time in 3D, inspired by a TikTok motion-capture video link the user supplied.

## Requirements
- Real-time 3D tracking of body, face, hands, feet, eyes, and mouth.
- App should work in browser preview, be visually polished, and support mobile touch layouts.
- Keep tracking local; video should not be uploaded.
- TikTok reference (`https://vt.tiktok.com/ZSgTJ8uek/`) was unavailable, so design is an original interpretation.

## Decisions
- Use MediaPipe Tasks Vision (`PoseLandmarker`, `FaceLandmarker`, `HandLandmarker`) with Three.js neon rig.
- Feet from pose landmarks 27–32; eyes/mouth from face landmarks + 52 blendshapes.
- Synthetic demo mode for camera-free use and screenshot verification.
- Vendor WASM/models locally; Vite with `--base ./`; lazy-load `src/tracking.js` on camera start.
- Use procedural demo face/hand/body animation; no external GLB assets.
- Renderer now `alpha: true`, transparent clear, CSS radial-gradient studio background; antialias off for performance.
- Pip canvas reduced to `300 × 200`, drawn at 15 fps with cached background and no canvas shadows; UI updates throttled to 140 ms.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite app scaffolded with `three@0.187.0`, `@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.2.0`, `vite@8.3.5`; local WASM/models/fonts under `public/`.
- Full HUD shell, tracking matrix, face signals, energy graph, layers, input controls, PIP, mobile matrix/dock, loader, toast implemented.
- Demo mode renders body, procedural face mesh, hands, feet, particles, ground, and HUD; loader hides correctly.
- Removed expensive full-screen `.ambient`, `.grain`, `.scanlines`, `.vignette` layers and continuous ambient animation.
- Fixed performance bottleneck: PIP canvas was dominant (~2.9 → ~13 fps under SwiftShader); removed shadowBlur, cached background/scanlines, reduced resolution and update rate.
- Fixed face orientation (head basis now uses `p[8] - p[7]`, so +Z faces camera).
- Improved avatar: slimmer bones/joints, lathe torso with broad chest, wireframe pelvis, larger head, low-poly head shell, face renderOrder above head shell, shortened neck, larger demo hands, narrower feet.
- Added responsive camera fit for portrait/mobile (`z = 5.15`), smaller mobile PIP, mobile chip fade mask.
- Fixed camera-error loader bug: progress callback now guarded by `active` flag.
- Fixed real FaceRig bugs: `this.real.tess` wrapper and `const { pointPositions, pointGeo } = this.real`.
- Verified real camera path with fake getUserMedia streams: pose detection works (photo), face detection works (portrait), both pose+face render together, no console TypeError.
- `npm run build` succeeds: `dist/assets/index-*.js` ~627 kB, `tracking-*.js` ~160 kB, CSS ~19 kB.
- Final demo screenshots captured at desktop (1050×793) and mobile (390×844).
- Removed temporary `public/test-pose.jpg` and `public/test-portrait.jpg`.

### Active
- Final visual polish and validation. Current tuned demo screenshot at `screenshots/tune-01.png` shows darker, more metallic limbs and reduced torso wire opacity; this tuning was applied at runtime via `window.__kinetic`, not yet written into source.

### Blocked
- None currently.

## Next Move
1. Decide whether to keep the runtime-tuned look (`boneMaterial.emissiveIntensity=0.3`, `metalness=0.9`, `roughness=0.18`, `wireMaterial.opacity=0.14`) and commit those values to `src/avatar.js`.
2. Verify final desktop/mobile screenshots after the tuning, including loader hidden and no console errors.
3. Re-test production build and optionally serve `dist/` with `vite preview` to confirm relative asset/WASM/model paths work.
4. Run final `npm run build`, capture final screenshots, and ensure no test artifacts remain.
5. Confirm mobile layout at 390×844 and desktop at 1050×793; check camera error path still hides loader.

## Relevant Files
- `src/avatar.js`: scene, renderer, body rig, torso/head geometry, camera fit, layers, snapshot.
- `src/face-rig.js`: real + demo face mesh, renderOrder, fixed tessellation/point buffers.
- `src/pip.js`: optimized input preview canvas.
- `src/tracking.js`: MediaPipe init, camera, inference, gaze/blendshape metrics.
- `src/main.js`: loop, demo/camera switching, model loading, `window.__kinetic` debug surface.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD updates, cached DOM writes, energy graph.
- `src/demo.js`: synthetic full-body/face/hand motion generator.
- `src/hand-rig.js`: hand skeleton with demo scale support.
- `src/foot-rig.js`: foot capsule rendering.
- `src/style.css`: HUD styling, responsive mobile layout, studio background.
- `index.html`: app shell and DOM.
- `src/filters.js`: One Euro/Vec3/Landmark filters.
- `src/glow.js`: shared glow textures/materials.
- `public/models/`, `public/wasm/`: local MediaPipe assets.
- `screenshots/`: verification images (`desktop-08.png`, `mobile-03.png`, `camera-face-02.png`, `tune-01.png`).

## Important Context
- Dev server runs in tmux session `kinetic` at `http://localhost:3000`.
- Playwright browser session `kinetic` is fresh at 1050×793, demo mode, ~11 fps under SwiftShader; earlier sessions had fake-camera init scripts but were closed/reopened.
- Under SwiftShader: demo ~10–13 fps, camera CPU inference ~1 fps / ~1000+ ms latency. Real GPU hardware expected much faster.
- `window.__kinetic` exposes `{ mode, trackerReady, frame, avatar, ui, pip, demo }`.
- Renderer: `alpha: true`, `setClearColor(0x04070c, 0)`, `scene.background = null`, antialias off, ACES tone mapping.
- Camera basis: `xAxis = p8 - p7`, `zAxis = xAxis × upHint`, `yAxis = zAxis × xAxis`; head radius `earDistance * 0.78`, clamp `0.078–0.155`.
- Face group renderOrder = 20; head mesh renderOrder = 0; head wire = 1.
- Real camera test used fake canvas streams; camera error path shows toast and hides loader with `trackerReady: true` after models load.
- Changes are uncommitted; repo was initially empty except scaffolding.

import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {

<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## KINETIC — Motion Lab

A real-time 3D motion-capture studio that runs entirely in the browser. MediaPipe Tasks
Vision tracks the full body, face, hands, feet, eyes and mouth, and a neon Three.js rig
mirrors the result live.

### Features

- **Full-body pose** — 33 landmarks, including feet and toe points.
- **Face mesh** — 478 landmarks with iris tracking plus 52 blendshapes for blink, jaw and smile.
- **Hands** — up to two 21-point hand skeletons.
- **Gaze, blink, jaw, smile and motion-energy readouts** in the HUD.
- **Synthetic demo loop** so the scene works without a camera.
- **Local by design** — video never leaves the device; models and WASM are served from `public/`.

### Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
npm run build    # static output in dist/
npm run preview  # serve the production build
```

### Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `C` | Start / stop the camera |
| `D` | Return to the demo loop |
| `R` | Reset the camera view |
| `S` | Save a frame as PNG |
| `F` | Toggle fullscreen |
| `1`–`6` | Toggle scene layers |
| Drag / scroll | Orbit / zoom the rig |

Camera access requires a secure context (`localhost` or HTTPS). On mobile, use the dock at
the bottom of the screen; the tracking matrix collapses into a compact chip row.
